summary: Review ten material upstream changes spanning reconstruction exactness, measured FPGA runtime variants, original-homebrew rendering, emulator failure paths and multi-platform build claims.
notes: The CPU audit queue contained zero unresolved source/target CPU areas, so no speculative architecture work was created. This pass adds two measured ND-120 Tang Nano 20K runtime variants and preserves explicit unknowns elsewhere. No upstream software, FPGA core, game or emulator was built, launched or played by the tracker.

project.status: Active incomplete browser remake; current work adds measured cross-backend villager load and grip checks and fixes a truncated WebGPU regression signature. The tracker did not run the browser build.

identity.narrative: README identifies a from-scratch 3D remake of the 1985 Ozark Softscape game. TypeScript economy implementation calculates treasures, regional trading and ferry passages; the tree includes world, movement, settlement, survival, state and test modules. Vite/React/Three.js package provides build, unit-test and browser-verification scripts. Scope/status: active proof of concept; explicitly incomplete. Metadata and selected file blobs were reviewed; this is not an exhaustive source audit.

classification.narrative: The repository remains an incomplete browser reimplementation of The Heart of Africa. The measured villager and renderer work does not establish binary-derived source recovery or relabel this project as a decompilation.

source_cpu.narrative: Primary identity evidence establishes the historical C64 game subject and the remake lineage. It does not explicitly establish the original executable CPU or show a verified original-binary CPU analysis. source_cpu remains empty; no 6510/Z80 value is inferred from platform names or the new implementation language.

target_cpu.narrative: React/Three.js/Vite and browser scripts establish a browser output, but neither TypeScript nor WebGPU identifies a host CPU architecture; target_cpu remains empty.

build.narrative: Upstream's bounded WebGPU charge fix now reads the preserved prefix of a 200-character-truncated measurement so the known 180-second water-stand failure remains charged. Other commits in the reviewed window add cross-backend villager dress, basket and head-load checks. These are upstream regression results; the tracker did not build, launch or play the remake.
build.limitations: The project remains incomplete, and no tracker-side runtime or visual comparison was performed.

runtime_profiles.narrative: README requires Node.js 20+ for development and describes WebGPU rendering with WebGL 2 fallback and lazy-loaded Kokoro TTS. These software/graphics capabilities establish no minimum CPU or RAM; no hardware runtime profile is asserted.

relationships.narrative: No current same-title/alias project found in title, subjects, upstream name, repository and notes comparison; metadata reports non-fork. Current primary documentation records bounded startup/runtime coverage for DM1 on DOS, Atari ST, Amiga and FM Towns; CSB on Amiga, Atari ST and FM Towns; and DM2 on DOS, Amiga, FM Towns and Macintosh. The latest receipts correct DM1 Amiga HD and DM2 FM Towns boot assertions and expand the cross-game startup matrix and diagnostics. These source-owned handoffs do not establish full campaign, save, display or audio parity; Nexus and Theron's Quest remain explicitly bounded, with authentic level/campaign consumers still incomplete. identity.narrative: A reconstruction of the 1988 Norsk Data ND-120 3202D CPU board from original design documents, first represented in Logisim and now maintained as Verilog. Includes CPU/decode gate arrays, PAL translations, microcode, MMU and bus devices, simulation harnesses and FPGA board integrations. This is a hardware/firmware reconstruction distinct from the catalogued nd100x and nd500x software emulators.

classification.narrative: Actual board-independent core and CPU/peripheral instantiation inspected. README claims SINTRAN III boots on Tang Nano, Nexys and MiSTer; MEGA65 bitstreams are timing-clean but not yet run on real MEGA65. Treat hardware claims as upstream reports. Root MIT licence inspected. Original 1988 design scans, firmware and other inherited material require their own provenance assessment.

source_cpu.narrative: Reconstructed architecture is ND-120 from original schematics, PAL equations and microcode.

target_cpu.narrative: Logical CPU in generated FPGA bitstream remains ND-120. FPGA vendor silicon and simulator C++ host are not claimed as native instruction-set output.

build.narrative: Primary documentation records measured Tang fast20 results: SMD plus Winchester fails routing even after removing the tape reader, while SMD-only and default Winchester variants route and boot SINTRAN. These upstream hardware results support compilable/runnable for documented variants; the tracker did not synthesize or boot the core.

runtime_profiles.narrative: Two Tang Nano 20K runnable variants are captured from measured primary documentation: SMD plus tape reader boots SINTRAN from 21540& in 26 seconds, and Winchester plus tape reader boots from 20500&. The same source explicitly says combined SMD+Winchester does not route on Tang, so that combination is not represented as runnable.
runtime_profiles.limitations: These are verified FPGA board/build combinations, not proof of a lowest compatible FPGA, RAM minimum or universal timing margin.
